label: Product engineering
title: From maintenance request to operating system
excerpt: AIRIA and AURA began with legacy modernization and became a connected operating environment for investment, trading, research, reporting, advisory, compliance and operations.
body: The useful question was not how to patch one workflow. It was how the firm’s workflows, data and decisions should connect.
That shift in scope turned a maintenance assignment into a production platform spanning front end, back end, APIs, mobile, dashboards, pipelines, security, deployment and product design.

label: Applied AI
title: Financial AI should know when to ask
excerpt: A useful model in a regulated environment needs boundaries, secure retrieval and the ability to ask a clarifying question when certainty is low.
body: General language models can be unsafe in financial operations when they invent an answer or expose sensitive context. The system has to narrow the task before it generates.
AURA uses controlled retrieval, constrained workflows and clarification behavior so uncertainty becomes visible instead of being hidden behind confident prose.

label: Architecture
title: What a fifty-dollar model budget forces you to learn
excerpt: A small initial monthly model budget made architecture, caching, retrieval quality and task boundaries more important than brute-force inference.
body: The initial model budget was about fifty dollars a month. That constraint rewarded careful context selection, bounded calls and workflows that only used a model where it added value.
Cost discipline was not separate from product quality. It led to a system that was easier to reason about, easier to govern and practical to operate.
